thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: spike in 5xx rate observed on /v1/generate (us-west-2). Alerting eng-oncall. Initial 5m error rate 6.2%, p95 latency rising. Paging @ryan_oncall and @sam_sre.
ryan_oncall: on it. I see the spike correlated with a burst of long-context requests from a handful of keys. Starting triage.
sam_sre: grabbing traces. any obvious infra change?
ana_infra: no infra deploys in last hour. GPU utilization ~92% on a subset of nodes, queue length spiked. Looks like we hit batching limits and backpressure is creating timeouts.
ryan_oncall: customer impact? product? maya_product?
maya_product: support is reporting multiple customers with timeouts and degraded streaming. Not yet a P1 but several enterprise customers saying requests hang ~10-20s.
liz_support: summary from support: 3 active CS tickets (customer A/B/C) - high-traffic endpoints for chat features. Customers are moved to retry loops.
ana_infra: logs show continuous_batching buffer growth; batch_timeout_ms = 20 currently, max_batch_tokens = 128, max_batch_size = 64. Under this burst those caps cause many small batches that overload GPU kernels. If we increase batch_timeout_ms and batch_size caps, we can pack more tokens per kernel call and reduce kernel overhead -> drop CPU/GPU scheduling pressure and lower 5xx. But that will increase tail latency for individual requests.
sam_sre: agreed. tradeoff: more throughput, higher tail latency. For live mitigation we can: 1) enable a temporary "high-throughput" batching profile that sets batch_timeout_ms=80, max_batch_tokens=512, max_batch_size=256; 2) apply per-key rate limiting for free-tier keys to preserve capacity for paid customers; 3) disable some noncritical features that amplify tokens (e.g., auto-summarize pipeline) for a short window.
ryan_oncall: prioritize protecting enterprise SLAs. Suggest step 1 + 2 now. We'll monitor error rate and p95.
ana_infra: I can push the batching profile to the serving pool for us-west-2-dev and then promote to prod nodes. Command I use:
```
# promote batching profile
redwoodctl config apply --cluster us-west-2 --profile high-throughput-batching
```
Profile contents (temp):
```
continuous_batching: true
batch_timeout_ms: 80
max_batch_size: 256
max_batch_tokens: 512
kernel_select: aggressive
```
ryan_oncall: do it. add a canary to 5% of capacity first.
nana_infra: rolling canary started -> deploy-bot: canary started on pool:usw2-prod-pool-3 (5%).
deploy-bot: canary deployment initiated by ana_infra at 2173456850.
ryan_oncall: watching metrics. sam, can you add quota throttles?
sam_sre: applying soft quotas to free-tier keys: reduce QPS to 0.5 and lower per-minute tokens to 2000 using rate-limit service. Command:
```
ratelimitctl update --selector tier=free --qps 0.5 --burst 5 --tokens-per-minute 2000
```
Applied.
liz_support: notifying impacted customers via templated message: "We've implemented temporary changes to improve stability; you may see slightly higher latency. We're monitoring." Will escalate any enterprise pushback.
maya_product: tagging affected customers: CustomerA (high), CustomerB (med), CustomerC (med). Keep me in loop.
ryan_oncall: canary looks ok for ~2m, error rate down from 6.2% -> 1.1% on canary nodes, GPU queue length down. p95 increased from 280ms -> 620ms on canary. Overall tradeoff acceptable for now.
sam_sre: rolling to 30% now. Rolling to 30% -> deploy-bot: rollout to 30% at 2173456872.
nana_infra: note: this profile increases per-request latency for small requests but absorbs long-context heavy tokens better by batching them into fewer kernel calls.
ryan_oncall: after 30% stabilize, move to 70% if errors continue to fall. Also keep rate-limits tight on free-tier.
liz_support: we are seeing a drop in new complaints. tickets not growing.
sam_sre: at 70% (deploy-bot reported at 2173456888) error rate across pool dropped to 0.4%, overall p95 ~720ms. CPU and GPU stalls reduced. No increase in OOMs.
ryan_oncall: good. hold here 10m then reevaluate. Maya, product decision on keeping this config?
maya_product: suggest keeping for the remainder of the traffic spike (unknown duration). We'll run post-incident analysis on cost impact. For now prioritize stability.
sam_sre: action items:
- [x] Enable canary high-throughput batching (5% -> 30% -> 70%)
- [x] Apply free-tier soft quotas
- [x] Disable auto-summarize pipeline for non-enterprise keys (defer may need config toggle)
- [ ] Monitor for regressed accuracy or customer complaints
- [ ] Prepare rollback steps (restore batch_timeout_ms=20, caps back to previous)
ryan_oncall: rolling mitigation saved the cluster. I'm going to handoff to Sam for monitoring. If errors spike again -> roll back profile and re-evaluate.
ryan_oncall: @sam_sre taking over oncall for next 2 hours. I will update schedule.
sam_sre: taking over. I'll watch error rates, p99 latency, and kernel metrics. If any enterprise SLA sees >3% errors escalate to P1.
liz_support: I'll keep customers updated and consolidate any escalations to product.
nana_infra: logging the config change in the runbook and tagging with incident id INC-2026-2173. Runbook note:
```
mitigation: high-throughput-batching
reason: burst of long-context requests causing kernel overhead -> high 5xx
start_ts: 2173456848
profile: continuous_batching: true; batch_timeout_ms: 80; max_batch_size: 256; max_batch_tokens: 512
rate_limits: free-tier reduced
```
ryan_oncall: final note: postmortem owners: sam_sre (exec), ana_infra (infra root cause), maya_product (customer impact). Assigning ticket.
sam_sre: acknowledged. I'll draft a timeline and attach traces and a diff of kernel invocation rates.
ryan_oncall: thanks team. Handoff complete.
sam_sre: (later) p99 still ok, error rate stable ~0.3%. I'll start a 4hr monitoring window and write up mitigation details.
liz_support: customers informed; CustomerA accepted the mitigation but asked for a detailed root-cause followup.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: 5xx rate returned to baseline. Closed by sam_sre at 2173456909."
